name: RAPPstore — official
description: Public catalog of rapplications. Each rapplication is a converged single-file agent.py produced by the double-jump loop. Pull into your local brainstem's agents/ directory and it works. Optional .egg pack restores example workflow state.
install_protocol: drop the singleton .py file into your local brainstem's `agents/` dir. Then POST /api/swarm/deploy with a bundle that includes it, OR: simply hot-load it from disk if your brainstem watches the agents/ folder. The file is everything — no install script, no pip, no native deps.

rapplications.name: BookFactory
rapplications.summary: Five-persona content pipeline (Writer → Editor → CEO → Publisher → Reviewer). One call, one chapter back.
rapplications.tagline: Source material in, publishable chapter out — 8 LLM calls under one POST.
rapplications.egg_note: No pre-populated state .egg shipped — BookFactory is stateless per call. Output artifacts are written to the workspace dir specified per call.

rapplications.name: SpineDAG
rapplications.summary: Universal Directed-Acyclic-Graph analyser. Point it at any folder, code project, Excel workbook, JSON/YAML config, or block of prose; it builds the dependency graph, finds hubs, leaves, orphans, cycles, and the critical path, scores Spine Health 0-100, and returns Markdown with a Mermaid diagram, ASCII tree, and a <spine-dag-json> envelope a UI can render.
rapplications.tagline: Map the spine of anything in 30 seconds — code, Excel, JSON, prose.
rapplications.egg_note: Stateless — no shipped state. Each call analyses a fresh target.

rapplications.name: WildhavenCEO

Wraps the pattern from kody-w/wildhaven-ceo: 'talk to the workspace' as the whole interface — no reading files, no learning the org, the agent does that for you.
rapplications.tagline: Talk to your workspace.
rapplications.egg_note: Stateless per call. The workspace context is supplied at invoke time; no shipped state.

rapplications.name: Vibe Coding Loop
rapplications.summary: Ship batches of 10 single-file HTML demos to a Jekyll site via parallel sub-agents. The orchestrator never writes demo code; it dispatches workers, wraps results, ships.
rapplications.tagline: One paragraph in, ten working browser demos out — in parallel.

rapplications.name: Cockpit
rapplications.summary: Local-first control plane for SSH-reachable hosts. Chat agent + HTTP backplane + browser UI on one local state dir. One operator drives N remote machines; nothing leaves the box.
rapplications.tagline: One terminal. N continuums. Zero leaks.
rapplications.egg_note: Stateless catalog entry. Operator state (host inventory, audit log) lives in ~/.cockpit/ and is portable via the export_state / import_state actions.
rapplications.access_note: Source files live in kody-w/RAPP_Store_Private. Unauthenticated raw fetches return HTTP 404. With a PAT scoped for read on the private repo, every URL returns 200 and the rapp installs normally.

rapplications.name: Thoughtbox
rapplications.summary: Local-first reflection journal — append, list, search, tag, export, import. Stateless agent, workspace-backed state, portable JSON blob you control.
rapplications.tagline: A box for your thoughts. Local-first, portable, yours.

rapplications.name: AgentTeam
rapplications.summary: The persona-routing brain of Bill Whalen's Agent Team Starter Kit, ported to a single rapplication. Given a project goal, returns the outcome frame, persona route, paste-ready GitHub issue body, and the needs-you questions the team would surface.
rapplications.tagline: Plan a project the way the kit would.
rapplications.egg_note: Stateless per call. Plans are returned in the response envelope; no shipped state.

rapplications.name: CoE Starter Kit
rapplications.summary: Bill Whalen's Agent Team (BWAT) starter kit as one rapplication. Run it and it bootstraps an outcome-first delivery team into your brainstem — Outcome Framer, Intake, Outcome Validator, PM, and Bill's twin — each pulled over HTTPS and sha256-pinned. Self-contained, stdlib-only.
rapplications.tagline: Stand up an outcome-first agent team in one drop.
rapplications.egg_note: Bootstraps the team on run (fetch + sha256-pin into your agents/ dir); no shipped state.

rapplications.name: rapp-god Forum
rapplications.summary: The agentic forum for the full RAPP stack — a threaded discussion forum where people and agents talk through the whole thing end to end (brainstem, kited layer, RACon, commons, registry, agents, governance). Mirrors the RAPP Commons pattern (rapp-commons-protocol/2.0, forum profile): your rappid is your handle, every post is signed, and it's held up by a kited vTwin that can graduate to an always-on cloud host.
rapplications.tagline: Discuss the whole stack — your handle is your key.
rapplications.egg_note: No shipped state — the forum is a live signed stream. The UI mints your rappid locally and connects to the always-on cloud host (or falls back to a kited host).

rapplications.name: RAPP Commons
rapplications.summary: A contribution app for the RAPP Commons — the stack-agnostic social network for agents. Mint a rappid (your username is your key), then post to a signed, append-only stream that's held up by an ephemeral kited vTwin host at a well-known address. No sign-up, no server, no account: the key is the account. Implements rapp-commons-protocol/2.0 — anyone, any stack, can step through the front door and contribute.
rapplications.tagline: Post to the agents' social network — your key is your username.
rapplications.egg_note: No shipped state — the Commons is a live signed stream you join over WebRTC. The UI mints your rappid locally (the key never leaves your device) and connects to the well-known kited host.

rapplications.name: Project Tracker
rapplications.summary: A local-first tracker for a portfolio of AI-agent projects and their MVP statements. The web UI is a 1:1 clone of the aibast-agents-library project-tracker tool; the bundled ProjectTracker agent manages the same portfolio headlessly over /chat. Both speak the tool's native projectTrackerData JSON, so exports and imports round-trip with it. Self-contained and stdlib-only: the UI works offline via localStorage, and unifies with the agent's on-device store when the rapplication's local server is running.
rapplications.tagline: Track AI-agent projects and their MVPs, local-first — a web UI plus a headless agent over one JSON.

rapplications.name: Novell

rapplications.name: RAPP Crispy
rapplications.summary: Native macOS 14+ meeting app with graphical record/stop/cancel, app-owned microphone permissions, explicitly named Apple AVFoundation voice processing, bundled local Whisper transcription, meeting history and audio/transcript views. Optional screen/window capture is video only. Notes stay disabled until a provider is selected, approved and requested. Existing Python/CLI integration remains secondary; DeepFilterNet, RNNoise and compatible loopback routing are optional unbundled legacy paths, not the native default.
rapplications.tagline: Native local meeting capture and transcription, with explicit enhancement choices and consent-gated notes.

produced_by.method: Historical secondary single-file-agent and UI integration; native release details are in desktop

rapplications.egg_note: The existing egg is a retired historical hatch cartridge, not the native 1.5.0 installer. It has not been regenerated or presented as this release. Use the architecture-specific desktop ZIP; singleton and UI paths remain optional source integration.

prerequisites: macOS 14.0 or later. Choose arm64 for Apple Silicon or x86_64 for Intel. The native app includes the local CPU whisper-cli runtime; no Homebrew, Terminal, Python or local ASR server is required for native capture/transcription.

Grant Microphone access to RAPP Crispy only when starting a recording. Screen Recording access is optional and requested only when explicitly selecting a display or window. Obtain participants' permission before recording.
Select and download a verified Base English or Small English speech model in Settings. Internet access is needed for that model-data download; meeting content is not uploaded to the model host.

Native enhancement is Apple AVFoundation voice processing, not DeepFilterNet or RNNoise. Optional advanced paths require a separately selected trusted deep-filter 0.5.6 executable or ffmpeg with arnndn and a .rnnn model; those components are not bundled.

A compatible existing loopback device is optional only for separately configured legacy crispy live routing. The native app neither installs a driver nor implements live virtual-microphone routing or system/far-end audio capture.

A notes-provider executable is optional. Missing provider or consent does not block local audio/transcription; cloud-capable providers receive transcripts only after explicit approval and a notes request.
desktop.privacy: Nothing records on launch. The app captures only the selected microphone after Record; stop/cancel and active state are visible. Optional explicitly selected screen/window capture is silent video, not remote-participant or system audio. Apple voice processing and Whisper transcription run locally. Existing meetings, audio and transcripts remain under ~/.rappcrispy/meetings; interrupted jobs preserve completed files. Model downloads fetch checksum-verified public model data without uploading meeting content. Notes are disabled until a provider and destination are reviewed, approved and requested; the example Claude hook sends authorized transcripts to Anthropic. Consent is bound to the provider configuration/executable and can be revoked, but already transmitted content cannot be recalled. A user-selected local hook is not a network sandbox. Native Apple processing is not labeled RNNoise/DeepFilterNet, and legacy benchmark results are not attributed to it. Publisher release reports bind the downloadable bytes and app checks; they are not independent Apple certification or RAPP/1 acceptance by the Store.
setup: Download the architecture-specific ZIP from the v1.5.0 release. Double-click it in Finder and drag RAPPCrispy.app to Applications.
Launch RAPP Crispy from Applications and let normal macOS/Gatekeeper checks run; do not bypass system protections. Nothing captures automatically.
In Settings, choose a speech model and click Download verified model. Recording can proceed before a model is available; saved audio can be transcribed later.
Choose the microphone and enhancement mode, then click Record. Approve the app's Microphone permission when prompted; use Stop & process or Cancel job to finish.
For optional screen video, enable it and explicitly choose the display/window before recording. This does not add system or far-end audio.
Browse Meetings to play audio and read actual transcripts/notes. Configure and approve a notes provider only if desired, then explicitly request notes.
desktop.agent_integration: The Python singleton and local UI are secondary integrations, not native installers. Installing a .py file does not install RAPPCrispy.app, Whisper or macOS permissions. With a native app installed, record/run actions prepare visible controls and require the user to press Record; doctor/live_status use read-only native diagnostics. File-based list/read and legacy commands remain available. CRISPY_BACKEND=legacy explicitly selects old headless capture, which needs its own ffmpeg, models and local whisper server. DeepFilterNet/RNNoise and loopback paths remain optional, unbundled legacy/developer dependencies. Native notes approval is separate from legacy CRISPY_NOTES_CONSENT=1; neither path enables cloud notes by default. The immutable native-build source differs from this later metadata/integration commit; federation must pin integration URLs to the published metadata commit. Retired eggs are not part of the native install.

rapplications.name: RAPP Rewind
rapplications.summary: Native macOS searchable screen memory with explicit Start/Pause/Stop, app-owned ScreenCaptureKit, on-device Vision OCR, and local SQLite FTS5. Capture, OCR, indexing, and search stay on this Mac; optional RAPP host integration is separate.
rapplications.tagline: A local, searchable memory of everything that has been on your screen.

prerequisites: macOS 14.0 or later; choose arm64 for Apple silicon or x86_64 for Intel.
Screen Recording permission must be granted to RAPP Rewind itself after pressing Start; Terminal and Python grants are not inherited.
No additional tools, models, cloud account, Python, ffmpeg, Homebrew, microphone permission, or Accessibility permission are required for the native app.
Optional singleton/twin integration requires a Python-compatible RAPP host plus the separately installed native app, or an explicitly selected compatibility rewind CLI with its own dependencies.
desktop.privacy: Capture is opt-in: RAPP Rewind requests its own Screen Recording grant only after Start and never records automatically at launch or login. ScreenCaptureKit capture, Vision OCR, fingerprints, SQLite indexing, and search stay on this Mac; no audio is captured and this processing path makes no network upload. Images, OCR text, and the index remain in ~/.rapprewind or an explicit REWIND_HOME. Visible content can include passwords and private messages; configure and save bundle-ID/window-title exclusions or pause before sensitive work. Rewind does not encrypt its files; protect the account and use FileVault. Image retention is off until enabled, and pruning keeps indexed text. Background operation and idle-at-login launch are separate explicit opt-ins. The optional RAPP host conversation may forward text returned by its agent to that host's LLM; use the native app or direct CLI when that conversation is not appropriate.
setup: Download the versioned ZIP matching your Mac: arm64 for Apple silicon or x86_64 for Intel.
Double-click the ZIP in Finder to extract RAPPRewind.app, then drag the application to Applications.
Launch RAPP Rewind from Applications. No Terminal installer, Python setup, signing credentials, or security bypass is required.

Review Privacy & Settings, add and save exclusions if needed, then press Start to request Screen Recording for RAPP Rewind. If macOS requests a restart, quit and reopen the app before pressing Start again.
Use the visible Pause/Stop controls to stop collection. Search or select moments in the native timeline. Preview and confirm image pruning yourself; indexed text remains searchable.
Open at Login opens idle. Keep running when the last window closes is a separate setting; both options are off by default and require explicit opt-in.
desktop.agent_integration: The native application is the primary download. The Python singleton/twin and web UI are secondary allowlisted integration for an existing RAPP host; dropping a .py file into a host does not install the macOS application. Install the native app separately. The adapter discovers it in Applications or through REWIND_NATIVE_APP and requires a successful Gatekeeper assessment; REWIND_CLI explicitly selects the legacy CLI instead. Native capture only reveals Start/Pause/Stop controls, doctor takes no screenshot, prune is always a preview, and bench uses generated pixels. The host's LLM conversation may receive agent search output. Existing twin port and protocol behavior are unchanged.

rapplications.egg_note: The copy of this manifest inside the .egg describes a hatch cartridge: it carries twin/ and state/ only. `agent` and `ui` are bundle-relative paths that live in the source repo, not in the egg — the twin loads twin/agents/, not singleton/.

rapplications.name: RAPP Voice
rapplications.summary: Native macOS dictation with local whisper.cpp recognition, a weighted dictionary, app-aware cleanup, and safe insertion or manual-copy fallback. Optional cloud polish is off until explicitly consented.
rapplications.tagline: Native, local dictation with safe insertion and manual-copy fallback.

prerequisites: macOS 14.0 or later; choose the arm64 ZIP for Apple Silicon or the x86_64 ZIP for an Intel Mac.
Microphone permission is required for recording that you explicitly start.
Internet access is needed to download a verified Base English or Small English speech model in Setup. Model weights are not included in the application ZIP; recognition works offline afterward.
Accessibility enables automatic cross-app input; Accessibility plus Input Monitoring enable the global shortcut. App buttons and Copy/manual-paste remain available without those grants.

No Hammerspoon, Homebrew, ffmpeg, localhost speech server, account, or API key is required for native local dictation. Optional polish needs a separately reviewed executable hook and explicit provider consent.
desktop.privacy: Capture starts only when you hold the shortcut or press Start. The app records through its own microphone permission, transcribes audio locally with bundled whisper.cpp, and deletes its audio work files after completion, errors, or cancellation. Native diagnostics retain counts and status, not transcripts. Settings, verified models, and work files use ~/Library/Application Support/io.rapp.voice; the existing ~/.rappvoice dictionary and legacy state are preserved. Downloads fetch model weights, not voice data. Secure Input, protected or changed fields, and missing permissions prevent automatic insertion and offer manual copy instead. Optional polish is off by default; only after reviewing the executable and named recipient and explicitly consenting can a triggered transcript be passed to that hook, which may send text to a provider such as Claude/Anthropic and incur charges. Audio is not passed to the polish hook. The secondary twin chat may separately use its host's LLM.
setup: Download the ZIP matching your Mac, expand it in Finder, and drag the extracted RAPPVoice.app into Applications.
Launch RAPP Voice from Applications and open Setup. Launching the app or granting a permission does not start a recording.
Enable Microphone when ready, choose Base English or Small English, and use Download / retry. Wait for model size and SHA-256 verification and save the selection.
For shortcuts across other apps and automatic insertion, grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring to RAPP Voice in System Settings, then refresh grants or reopen the app if macOS requests it.

Focus a normal text field, hold Right Command, speak, and release. Double-tap for hands-free recording; use Stop or Cancel as needed. Without suitable permissions or focus, review the transcript and choose Copy/manual-paste.
Change the shortcut, dictionary, or insertion method in the GUI. Keep optional polish disabled unless you have reviewed its hook and recipient and explicitly consented.
desktop.agent_integration: The Python singleton and existing twin/UI are secondary integration, not a native installer. In a compatible RAPP/BasicAgent host they discover the installed RAPPVoice.app or the explicit RAPPVOICE_NATIVE_CLI path and send typed JSON to RAPPVoice --action. The existing doctor, dictionary, add_term, stats, and process actions inspect readiness, manage vocabulary, summarize status-only logs, or clean supplied text; none can record, inject input, or invoke polish. A .py drop does not install the app, its speech model, or macOS permissions. When no native executable is present, the existing Hammerspoon/localhost backend remains a legacy fallback; native failures are not replayed through that fallback.

rapplications.egg_note: The retained .egg is an unchanged legacy twin hatch cartridge, not the native 1.1.0 application or its installer. Native downloads are listed only in desktop.artifacts; current singleton/UI integration files live in the source repository.

rapplications.name: RAPP Shot
rapplications.summary: Capture, annotate and redact screenshots entirely on-device. Finds credentials in the pixels with Apple's Vision OCR and paints them out opaquely BEFORE the image is shared. Redaction is a solid fill, never a blur, because blur and pixelation are reversible often enough to have leaked real credentials.
rapplications.tagline: Capture, annotate and redact screenshots entirely on-device.

publish_your_own.summary: Author a rapplication using the multi-file source pattern (see blog/89). Run the double-jump loop until convergence (typically 1-3 cycles per content shape). Collapse to a singleton via tools/build-rapplication.py. Submit a PR adding an entry to rapp_store/index.json.

install_protocol_senses: Drop the *_sense.py file into your local brainstem at rapp_brainstem/senses/. Auto-discovered each chat request, no restart. Senses are TRANSLATIONS of the main response into different modes of expression (Constitution Article XXIV).
gated_rapplications_note: This catalog supports gated rapplications (SPEC §11). Entries with "access": "private" reference source files in a private GitHub repo; unauthenticated raw fetches return 404 by design. Clients must surface an auth-prompt and use a PAT scoped for read on the declared private_repo.
